html:
The Karapanã, who call themselves Muteamasa, are a Tukanoan people of the Vaupés region on the border of Colombia and Brazil. They live along rivers in the rainforest, in villages that were once single large longhouses called malocas.

They belong to a network of peoples, including the Tariana, the Desana and the Tuyuka, in which people must marry someone who speaks a different language. As a result, most people speak three or four languages. They farm bitter manioc, fish and hunt.

Rubber traders reached the Vaupés during the rubber boom, and Catholic and Protestant missions followed in the 1900s. See also Karapana.
